html:
The five principles that are the founding philosophy of Indonesia, first set out by Sukarno in a speech on 1 June 1945. The name comes from Sanskrit for "five principles".

In their usual order they are:

  • belief in one God,
  • just and civilised humanity,
  • the unity of Indonesia,
  • democracy led by wisdom through deliberation among representatives,
  • social justice for all Indonesians.

Sukarno spoke to a committee preparing for independence under Japanese occupation. The country was mostly Muslim but had Christian, Hindu and Buddhist regions, and he wanted a base that all could share. A draft called the Jakarta Charter added a clause requiring Muslims to follow Islamic law. It was dropped the day after Indonesia declared independence, to keep the Christian east inside the new state.

Pancasila made Indonesia neither an Islamic state nor a secular one. Under Suharto it was made compulsory, and every party and group had to adopt it as its sole principle. It is still taught in every school and invoked to defend the nation's diversity, as the Youth Pledge did before it.
sum: The five principles that are the founding philosophy of Indonesia, first set out by Sukarno in a speech on 1 June 1945. The name comes from Sanskrit for "five principles".
